sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 09.11.2021 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Srirangapatna in MVC No.95/2017.
This appeal is founded on the premises of inadequacy of compensation.
Hence, the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
That on 02.12.2016 at about 12.30 p.m., the claimant herein was a pillion rider along with one Mahesha riding a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-10-S-0451 when t h e y w e r e t r a v e l i n g f r o m K o l l e g a l a t o w a r d s N C : 2 0 2 4 : K H C : 6 3 8 2 Malavalli-Bengaluru side, near Anagalli, on Kollegala and Malavalli road, at that time, the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-42-F-520 came in a rash and negligent manner from opposite direction and dashed against the motor cycle of the claimant.
Due to the said impact, the claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, the claimant was shifted to Kollegala General Hospital wherein, he was admitted as an inpatient from 02.12.2016 to 21.12.2016 and underwent surgery.
The claimant spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenditure etc.
In view of injuries suffered and financial expenditure expended, he filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
3.1 It is stated that the claimant was hale and healthy prior to the occurrence of accident.

He was working as a mason and earning an income of Rs.15,000/-
per month.
Due to the occurrence of accident and injuries suffered, the claimant is unable to do his work normally as NC: 2024:KHC:6382 he was doing prior to the occurrence of accident.
Hence, the claimant filed a claim petition seeking compensation.

sentences.text: On service of notice, respondent-Corporation appeared through its counsel and filed statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition including age, avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
On the contrary pleaded that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle.
Hence, liability requires to be fastened on the rider of the motor cycle rather than against the KSRTC bus.
Hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.3 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

3.4 In order to substantiate issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P20 and the Doctor as CW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.C1 to C5.

On the NC: 2024:KHC:6382 other hand, respondent examined a witness as RW.1 and got marked document as Ex.R1.
3.5

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.5,73,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.

It also held that the medical bills do not carry any interest and respondent-Corporation was directed to pay the compensation amount along with interest and deposit the amount within one month from the date of the order.
3.6 Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement.

4. It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the tribunal has committed an error in awarding meagre compensation, NC: 2024:KHC:6382 which calls for interference at the hands of this Court.
Accordingly, he seeks enhancement of compensation.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Corporation contends that the tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference.
Hence, he seeks dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for appellant-claimant and learned counsel for respondent-Corporation, a short point that would arise for consideration:
"(i) Whether the claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?
7.

Having perused the impugned judgment and award, the occurrence of accident, involvement of vehicle and injuries suffered, the documents produced at Exs.P1 to P20, the Police records and medical records, out of which the Police records clearly depict the filing of FIR and laying of charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and same has not been challenged or controverted.
Therefore, the tribunal rightly attributed the negligence against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The medical records, which clearly depicts the injury sustained by the claimant in the occurrence of accident.

sentences.text: Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation, income and disability, it is stated that age of the claimant was 20 years as on the date of occurrence of accident.
The tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier at '18', which does not call for interference.

The tribunal taken the income of Rs.9,500/-
per month, in view of there being no proof of income and the same is retained.

9. CW.1-Doctor stated in his evidence with regard to the injuries sustained by the claimant and magnitude of the same and has opined the disability to the extent of 65% to a particular limb and he has not stated the disability to the whole body.
However, the tribunal has assessed the disability at 15%.

On the basis of age, avocation and the injuries sustained in the present case, though CW.1-Doctor has stated the disability to a NC: 2024:KHC:6382 particular limb at 65%, the same is divided by 1/3rd i.e., 21.66%.
Hence, 22% of disability would have to be taken as disability to the whole body as against 15% taken by the tribunal.
Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to the compensation of Rs.4,51,440/- (Rs.9,500/- x 12 x 18 x 22%) towards loss of future income as against Rs.3,07,800/- awarded by the tribunal.
10. The tribunal awarded Rs.20,000/- towards pain and suffering.
However, this Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- under this head.
11. The tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Considering the injuries suffered by the claimant, this Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.35,000/- under this head.

12. The tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period, whereas, the claimant was inpatient for 13 days and he would require atleast four months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal NC: 2024:KHC:6382 day to day activities.
Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.38,000/- (Rs.9,500/- x 4) under this head.

13. The tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/- towards conveyance, diet, attendant, food and nourishment,
whereas, the claimant was inpatient for 13 days, which does not call for interference and the same is retained.
14.
The tribunal awarded Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, which does not call for interference and the same is retained.
However, the same would incur interest, which has been negatived by the tribunal.

15. In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,89,440/- as against Rs.5,73,000/- as mentioned in the table below:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Loss of future income due to 4,51,440-00 disability Pain and suffering
50,000-00 Loss of amenities 35,000-00 Loss of income during laid up period 38,000-00
Conveyance, diet, attendant, food 15,000-00 and nourishment Future medical expenses 2,00,000-00
